title: SSC MTS & Havaldar — Full-Length Session I & II CBT Mock
subtitle: 90 Questions • 90 Minutes (45+45m) • 270 Marks • Session I (0 Neg) / Session II (-1 Neg)
description: Exact official SSC Multi-Tasking (Non-Technical) Staff & Havaldar CBT replica: Session I (40 Qs: 20 Numerical + 20 Reasoning, 45 min, +3 / 0 negative marking) followed by locked Session II (50 Qs: 25 General Awareness + 25 English, 45 min, +3 / -1 negative marking).
instructions: Exact SSC MTS & Havaldar revised pattern: 2 mandatory back-to-back sessions of 45 minutes each (90 minutes total, 90 questions, 270 maximum marks).
Session I (Qualifying — 45 min): 40 Questions (20 Numerical & Mathematical Ability + 20 Reasoning Ability). +3 marks per correct answer and ZERO negative marking.
Session II (Merit — 45 min): 50 Questions (25 General Awareness + 25 English Language & Comprehension). +3 marks per correct answer and -1 mark negative marking for every wrong answer.

mts_cloze_1.title: Cloze Test — Session II English (Q46 to Q50)
mts_cloze_1.content:
Read the following passage carefully and fill in each blank with the most appropriate word.

For centuries, stepwells across western and central India were engineered to __(1)__ precious monsoon rainwater. These cool stone reservoirs provided drinking water to communities throughout the __(2)__ summer season. Over recent decades, however, the expansion of piped municipal supply meant that many historic stepwells were __(3)__ and choked with silt. Today, local citizens and heritage architects are partnering to __(4)__ these architectural marvels so they can once again recharge urban __(5)__ reserves.

sections.name: Session I: Numerical & Reasoning (No Neg Marking)

questions.question: Simplify: $48 \div 6 \times 3 + 12 - 5$
What is $35\%$ of $240$?
Find the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of 18, 24, and 36.
questions.explanation: $18=2\times 3^2$, $24=2^3\times 3$, $36=2^2\times 3^2 \Rightarrow \text{LCM} = 2^3 \times 3^2 = 72$.

questions.question: If $x : 15 :: 12 : 20$, find the value of $x$.
questions.explanation: $20x = 15 \times 12 = 180 \Rightarrow x = 9$.

questions.question: The average of five consecutive odd numbers is 27. What is the largest of these five numbers?
questions.explanation: The middle (3rd) number is 27, so the numbers are 23, 25, 27, 29, 31. Largest = 31.

questions.question: A bicycle bought for ₹4,500 is sold for ₹5,040. Find the profit percentage.
A jacket marked at ₹2,500 is sold at a 16% discount. Find its selling price.
Find the simple interest on ₹3,600 at 8% per annum for 3 years.
questions.explanation: $\text{SI} = \frac{3600 \times 8 \times 3}{100} = 36 \times 24 = ₹864$.

questions.question: Ravi can finish a job in 20 days and Sumit can finish it in 30 days. Working together, in how many days will they complete the job?
questions.explanation: Combined time = $\frac{20 \times 30}{20 + 30} = \frac{600}{50} = 12$ days.

questions.question: A bus travels 210 km in 3 hours 30 minutes. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.explanation: Time = 3.5 hours. Speed = $\frac{210}{3.5} = 60\text{ km/h}$.

questions.question: The length and breadth of a rectangle are 18 cm and 12 cm respectively. Find its perimeter.
questions.explanation: Perimeter = $2(l + b) = 2(18 + 12) = 60\text{ cm}$.

questions.question: Find the volume of a right circular cylinder of radius $7\text{ cm}$ and height $10\text{ cm}$ ($\pi = \frac{22}{7}$).
questions.explanation: $V = \pi r^2 h = \frac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 \times 10 = 1,540\text{ cm}^3$.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is completely divisible by 11?
Find the amount on ₹5,000 at 10% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
Express the fraction $\frac{7}{8}$ as a percentage.
A train 150 m long crosses an electric pole in 6 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.explanation: Speed = $150/6 = 25\text{ m/s} = 25 \times \frac{18}{5} = 90\text{ km/h}$.

questions.question: Two vessels contain sugar solution of 30 litres (20% sugar) and 20 litres (30% sugar). When mixed together, what is the percentage of sugar in the resulting solution?
questions.explanation: Total sugar = $6 + 6 = 12$ L in 50 L total ⇒ $\frac{12}{50} \times 100 = 24\%$.

questions.question: The area of a square field is $625\text{ m}^2$. Find the length of its boundary (perimeter).
questions.explanation: Side = $\sqrt{625} = 25\text{ m}$. Perimeter = $4 \times 25 = 100\text{ m}$.

questions.question: The present ages of Aman and Vijay are in the ratio $4 : 5$. After 6 years, the ratio becomes $5 : 6$. What is Aman's present age?
questions.explanation: Each ratio part increases by 1 in 6 years ⇒ 1 unit = 6 years. Aman = $4 \times 6 = 24$ years.

questions.question:
Monthly sales of bicycles at a shop:

| Month | Units Sold |
|---|---|
| Jan | 45 |
| Feb | 55 |
| Mar | 60 |
| Apr | 80 |

What is the average monthly sale over the four months?

Find the missing number:
`5, 11, 17, 23, 29, ?`
questions.explanation: Constant difference of +6: $29 + 6 = 35$.

questions.question: If `PEN` is coded as `QFO`, how is `BOOK` coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts by +1: B→C, O→P, O→P, K→L ⇒ `CPPL`.

questions.question: `Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ?`
questions.explanation: A doctor works in a hospital; a teacher works in a school.

questions.question: Choose the odd one out from the given numbers.
questions.explanation: $27=3^3$, $64=4^3$, $125=5^3$ are perfect cubes, while $144=12^2$ is not a cube.

questions.question:
Find the missing letter-cluster:
`AB, DE, GH, JK, ?`
questions.explanation: Each cluster starts +3 from the previous start: A, D, G, J, M ⇒ `MN`.

questions.question:
If `+` means `×` and `-` means `÷`, find the value of:
`36 - 4 + 5`
questions.explanation: $36 \div 4 \times 5 = 9 \times 5 = 45$.

questions.question:
Statements:
1. All roses are flowers.
2. Some flowers are red.

Conclusions:
I. Some flowers are roses.
II. All roses are red.
questions.explanation: From Statement 1, 'Some flowers are roses' (I) definitely follows; no definite link exists between roses and red.

questions.question: Five friends P, Q, R, S, and T sit in a row facing North. R is exactly in the middle. P sits at the extreme left end. Q sits immediately to the right of R. S sits between P and R. Who sits at the extreme right end?
questions.explanation: Left to right: P (1), S (2), R (3), Q (4), T (5). Hence T sits at the extreme right end.

questions.question: Deepak is the brother of Ravi. Rekha is the sister of Atul. Ravi is the son of Rekha. How is Deepak related to Rekha?
questions.explanation: Deepak is Ravi's brother and Ravi is Rekha's son, so Deepak is also Rekha's Son.

questions.question: Sunil faces North. He turns $90^\circ$ clockwise, then $180^\circ$ anti-clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: North + $90^\circ$ CW = East; East + $180^\circ$ ACW = West.
Square relationship: $8^2 = 64$, so $11^2 = 121$.

questions.question: In a class of 35 students, Kavita ranks 9th from the top. What is her rank from the bottom?
questions.explanation: Rank from bottom = $35 - 9 + 1 = 27\text{th}$.

questions.question: If `BAT` = 23 and `CAT` = 24, then `MAT` = ?
questions.explanation: Sum of letter values: M(13) + A(1) + T(20) = 34.

questions.question: Which word comes FIRST in English dictionary order?
questions.explanation: `Pre-d(ict)` comes before `Pre-p(are)`, `Pre-s(ent)`, and `Pre-v(ent)`.

questions.question:
Find the missing number:
`2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?`
questions.explanation: Pattern $n(n+1)$: $1\times 2, 2\times 3, 3\times 4, 4\times 5, 5\times 6, 6\times 7 = 42$.

questions.question: Select the odd word out.
questions.explanation: Mercury, Venus, and Mars are planets; Moon is Earth's natural satellite.

questions.question: Four friends A, B, C, and D sit around a circular table facing the centre. A sits opposite to C. B sits immediately to the right of A. Who sits immediately to the left of A?
questions.explanation: Clockwise/anticlockwise around a 4-seat circle: A opposite C, B immediately right of A, so the only remaining seat (immediately left of A) is occupied by D.

questions.question: `Rupee : India :: Yen : ?`
questions.explanation: Rupee is India's currency; Yen is Japan's currency.

questions.question: Pick the odd letter-cluster out.
questions.explanation: ACE, GIK, and MOQ increase by +2 each step, whereas STU increases by +1.

questions.question:
Find the missing number:
`100, 95, 85, 70, 50, ?`

sections.name: Session II: General Awareness & English (-1 Neg Marking)

questions.question: How many Fundamental Rights are currently guaranteed by the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: There are 6 Fundamental Rights (Right to Property was removed from Part III by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978).

questions.question: Bihu is the principal harvest festival of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Bohag (Rongali), Kati, and Magh Bihu are the three signature festivals of Assam.

questions.question: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to its frequent course changes and devastating floods?
questions.explanation: The Kosi river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' (while Damodar was historically called 'Sorrow of Bengal').

questions.question: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi lead the famous Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha)?
questions.explanation: Gandhiji walked from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi from 12 March to 6 April 1930.

questions.question: Which vitamin is primarily synthesized in human skin upon exposure to sunlight?
questions.explanation: UVB rays convert 7-dehydrocholesterol in skin into Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol).

questions.question: What is the common name of Sodium Bicarbonate ($\text{NaHCO}_3$)?
questions.explanation: Sodium bicarbonate ($\text{NaHCO}_3$) is commonly known as Baking Soda.

questions.question: Sound waves CANNOT travel through which of the following media?
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical longitudinal wave requiring a material medium; it cannot propagate in vacuum.

questions.question: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Under Article 64 of the Constitution, the Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon (Dharmachakrapravartana) at which place?
questions.explanation: Buddha delivered his first sermon to five ascetics at the Deer Park in Sarnath near Varanasi.

questions.question: Kaziranga National Park is located in which state of India?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga National Park (UNESCO site) is located in Golaghat and Nagaon districts of Assam.

questions.question: Which apex bank acts as the 'Banker to the Government' and 'Lender of Last Resort' in India?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India (established 1 April 1935) is India's central bank.

questions.question: Who composed India's national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana'?
questions.explanation: Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore composed 'Jana Gana Mana', adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950.

questions.question: How many players are on the field for one team in a standard Field Hockey match?
questions.explanation: Each field hockey team fields 11 players (10 outfield + 1 goalkeeper).

questions.question: Who built the Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri to commemorate his victory over Gujarat?
questions.explanation: Emperor Akbar built the Buland Darwaza in 1575 CE to celebrate his conquest of Gujarat.

questions.question: Ustad Bismillah Khan was an iconic Indian musician renowned for playing which instrument?
questions.explanation: Bharat Ratna awardee Ustad Bismillah Khan popularized the Shehnai on global concert stages.

questions.question: Which organ in the human body filters waste products from the blood to produce urine?
questions.explanation: Nephrons inside the kidneys filter nitrogenous waste (urea) and excess water from blood.

questions.question: Which planet in our Solar System is known as the 'Red Planet'?
questions.explanation: Mars appears reddish due to iron oxide (rust) covering its surface.

questions.question: Which Part of the Indian Constitution deals with Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)?
questions.explanation: Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) contains the Directive Principles of State Policy.

questions.question: As per Census 2011, which Indian state had the highest population density (persons per sq km)?
questions.explanation: Bihar recorded the highest population density among Indian states at 1,106 persons per sq km (Census 2011).

questions.question: What is the pH value of pure neutral water at $25^\circ\text{C}$?
questions.explanation: Neutral solutions have pH = 7; acidic < 7; basic > 7.

questions.question: Who wrote the autobiography 'Wings of Fire'?
options: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
questions.explanation: 'Wings of Fire' is the celebrated autobiography of India's Missile Man and 11th President, Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

questions.question: Bharatanatyam is the traditional classical dance form of which state?
questions.explanation: Bharatanatyam originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: The Jallianwala Bagh Massacre took place in Amritsar on which date?
questions.explanation: General Dyer ordered troops to open fire on a peaceful Baisakhi gathering at Jallianwala Bagh on 13 April 1919.

questions.question: World Environment Day is observed globally every year on:
questions.explanation: World Environment Day is celebrated on 5 June (22 April is Earth Day; 16 Sept is World Ozone Day).

questions.question: Which Indian city is popularly known as the 'Pink City'?
questions.explanation: Jaipur (Rajasthan), founded by Sawai Jai Singh II, is famed as the Pink City and is a UNESCO World Heritage city.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate SYNONYM of: `RAPID`
questions.explanation: 'Rapid' means fast or swift.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of: `ANCIENT`
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'Ancient' is 'Modern'.

questions.question:
Select the one-word substitute for:
`One who does not believe in the existence of God`
questions.explanation: An 'Atheist' disbelieves in the existence of God.

questions.question:
Select the meaning of the idiom:
`A piece of cake`
questions.explanation: 'A piece of cake' refers to something very easy to accomplish.

questions.question:
Spot the grammatical error:
`The children / was playing / happily in / the garden.`
questions.explanation: 'Children' is plural, so it requires `were playing` instead of `was playing`.

questions.question: Please turn ______ the lights before leaving the classroom.
questions.explanation: `Turn off` is the correct phrasal verb meaning to switch off.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is `Separate` (with 'a' after 'p').

questions.question:
Substitute the bracketed segment:
`He has been working in this factory (from) 2018.`
questions.explanation: A definite starting point in time (`2018`) takes `since` (whereas a duration takes `for`).

questions.question: Select the SYNONYM of: `COURAGEOUS`
questions.explanation: 'Courageous' means brave and fearless.

questions.question: Select the ANTONYM of: `GENEROUS`
questions.explanation: 'Stingy' (unwilling to give or spend) is the antonym of 'Generous'.

questions.question:
Select the meaning of the idiom:
`Break the ice`
options: To initiate conversation in an awkward silence
questions.explanation: 'Break the ice' means to ease tension and begin friendly conversation.

questions.question:
Select the one-word substitute for:
`A person who loves books`
questions.explanation: A 'Bibliophile' is a collector or great lover of books.

questions.question:
Identify the segment with a grammatical error:
`He did not / went to / the market / yesterday evening.`
questions.explanation: `did not` is always followed by the base verb (V1): `did not go`.

questions.question: Honesty is ______ best policy.
questions.explanation: Superlative adjectives (`best`) take the definite article `the`.

questions.question: Select the CORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: `Environment` (en + vi + ron + ment) is the correct spelling.

questions.question:
Improve the bracketed part:
`She prefers coffee (than) tea in the morning.`
questions.explanation: The verb `prefer` takes the preposition `to` (`prefers coffee to tea`).

questions.question: Select the SYNONYM of: `DILIGENT`
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' means showing careful, persistent, and hardworking effort.

questions.question: Select the ANTONYM of: `EXPAND`
questions.explanation: 'Contract' (shrink or become smaller) is the opposite of 'Expand'.

questions.question: The train arrived ______ the station ten minutes ahead of schedule.
questions.explanation: We arrive `at` a specific point/place like a station or airport.

questions.question:
Select the meaning of the idiom:
`Under the weather`
questions.explanation: 'Under the weather' means feeling sick or slightly unwell.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank (1).
questions.explanation: Traditional stepwells were built to 'harvest' and store monsoon rainwater.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank (2).
questions.explanation: Stored rainwater supported villages during the 'dry' summer months.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank (3).
questions.explanation: With piped water supply, many stepwells were 'neglected' and fell into disrepair.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank (4).
questions.explanation: Civic groups are now working to 'restore' these heritage structures.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank (5).
questions.explanation: Desilted stepwells recharge local 'groundwater' tables.
